vectors.name: formats-xml/basic/interleaved-elements-preserve-order
vectors.comment: A map-of-arrays model cannot represent this interleaving; the edge list can. This is the whole reason the Document is an ordered edge list rather than a map -- confirmed against JSON's own parse of the equivalent {"m":[...]} shape, which cannot preserve this order at all.

vectors.name: formats-xml/basic/attributes-are-dropped-on-read
vectors.comment: Ledger entry DIV-3 (closed 2026-08-23; divergence-ledger numbering, not chapter 2's D-N rules): the attribute x="1" is gone -- there is no path from a Document edge back to an attribute, so writing never produces one either -- and that drop MUST now be reported via format.attribute-dropped (Sec8.3.8), not silent. Path is $.a: the element the attribute was lost from.

vectors.name: formats-xml/basic/namespace-prefix-is-dropped-on-read
vectors.comment: Ledger entry DIV-3 (closed 2026-08-23; divergence-ledger numbering, not chapter 2's D-N rules): a prefixed tag <ns:b> reads as the local name b, with the prefix and any namespace binding discarded -- reported via format.namespace-dropped (Sec8.3.8), not silent. Path is $.a.b: the element the prefix was lost from, using the same RecordName.label-style dotted path convention Sec8.4 defines for Schema/Document paths generally.

vectors.name: formats-xml/basic/multi-rooted-document-cannot-be-written
vectors.comment: An XML document has exactly one top-level element; a Document with several top-level edges (legal in JSON/YAML/TOML) has no XML spelling at all. This is exactly why the worked examples in every format page wrap the Order under a single top-level `order` key -- XML alone requires it.

vectors.name: formats-xml/basic/label-with-illegal-xml-characters-cannot-be-written
vectors.comment: A space is not legal in an XML name, and there is no single well-defined substitute -- sanitizing it means inventing content, and (confirmed separately) can even make two genuinely different labels collide into the same written tag with no way to detect it happened. The write fails, unconditionally, not just under strict -- this is not a format.* adjustment a caller can opt out of checking for.

vectors.name: formats-xml/basic/empty-internal-node-cannot-be-written
vectors.comment: An empty internal node (zero edges) and an empty-string leaf have no distinct XML spelling -- both would be written as the self-closing <x />, and confirmed live that reading it back always produces the empty-string leaf, never the empty internal node, with no diagnostic distinguishing the two cases that collided. The write fails, unconditionally, not just under strict -- same principle as the label and NaN cases above, not a format.* adjustment that still succeeds.

vectors.name: formats-xml/basic/string-with-a-c0-control-character-cannot-be-written
vectors.comment: The format.string-illegal-char condition from Sec8.3.8: XML 1.0 cannot represent a raw C0 control character other than tab, LF and CR, and there is no substitute spelling, so the write MUST fail unconditionally rather than drop or replace the character. U+0001 is a legal Document string value -- Sec2.2 places no such restriction on the model -- so this is a target-format limitation, reachable from a perfectly valid Document. Completes the Sec8.3.8 five: the null-unrepresentable, float-special, key-sanitized and shape-empty-ambiguous conditions were already covered by vectors elsewhere in this suite; this was the only one of the five with no test. Verified against the Python reference, which raises write.unsupported-value at exactly this path.

vectors.name: formats-xml/profile/doctype-declaration-is-refused
vectors.comment: The data-XML profile refuses any DOCTYPE declaration, on sight rather than on use -- this one declares a harmless element type and references nothing, and is still refused. Rejecting at the declaration is what makes the rule testable and the failure early; rejecting only when a DTD-defined entity is referenced would make it conditional on content. The path is $ because the refusal happens before any element is read, so there is no edge to name. Note this document is well-formed XML: the code is a format refusal, deliberately NOT a parse.* syntax error, so a user is not sent looking for a defect in a valid file. Before the profile was specified, ports disagreed: Python and Java refused DOCTYPE-bearing documents, Rust and Go silently skipped the declaration, TypeScript accepted it -- a Sec9.2 grammar-acceptance divergence this vector exists to close.

vectors.name: formats-xml/profile/non-predefined-entity-reference-is-refused
vectors.comment: Only XML's five predefined entities are in profile.   could only have been defined by a DTD, which the profile already refuses, so accepting the reference while refusing the declaration would be incoherent. Included as its own vector because a reader that rejects DOCTYPE by pattern-matching the prolog would still accept this.

vectors.name: formats-xml/profile/mixed-content-is-refused
vectors.comment: Text alongside child elements has no Document shape: an edge's target is a value or a node, never both (Sec2.3 D-4). The Python reference already enforced this and its error message already named 'the data-XML profile' -- a concept that existed in one implementation and nowhere in the spec until now, with no vector and an unregistered code. That is exactly the gap this vector and the profile section close together.

vectors.name: formats-xml/basic/carriage-return-written-as-numeric-character-reference
vectors.comment: XML mandates line-ending normalization on parse -- a literal \r byte and a literal \n byte, written as-is, are indistinguishable on read-back (confirmed live, this used to be format.string-cr-normalized, a lossy warning-severity adjustment). A numeric character reference is exempt from that normalization, so writing \r as  instead of a raw byte is genuinely lossless, not merely reported-as-lossy -- confirmed live that  survives a compliant parser and reads back as the exact original byte. No diagnostic is needed for this case at all once the writer does this. Per omnist-spec#52: this vector's expect.text is indented, matching the Python reference's own writer default, but that indentation is not itself normative (Sec8.5.3) -- a compact-output writer (e.g. omnist-go's) is equally conformant, and a harness MUST strip insignificant inter-tag whitespace from both sides before comparing, per the new rule in Sec8.5.3. The escaping (, not a raw byte) is what this vector actually tests; the indentation shown here is incidental.

vectors.name: formats-xml/encoding/doubled-leading-bom-is-rejected
vectors.comment: D-21: D-15 consumes exactly one leading U+FEFF and stops. The text that remains is parsed by this surface's own grammar, which admits no U+FEFF as content at offset zero, so the second mark is a syntax error. The position is 1:1 because it is computed on the text remaining after the strip. The other red surface, for the same reason as YAML: XML 1.0 permits a leading BOM and the parser strips one itself, so under D-15's strip a doubled mark disappears silently. Measured: the reference accepts this input and returns the same Document as the single-BOM form (DIV-4).
